描述_EN: this virupa is one of the largest and most spectacular surviving works belonging to a group of images produced at the chinese court during the early 15th century. close contacts at this time between the emperor yongle (1403-1424), who was himself a buddhist, and tibetan religious leaders, led to frequent diplomatic and religious exchanges. this figure represents the mahasiddha, or great yogic adept virupa, who lived in 9th century north india. visiting tibetans received similar, though usually much smaller images, which were intended to mark and cement such newly made alliances. such figures lived alone or with a consort and became renowned for their unconventional lifestyles.they were revered in tibet as enlightened beings and often feature in tibetan lineages as the teachers of tibetans who journeyed to india to receive buddhist initiation.
描述_ZN: 此佛像是现存最大、最壮观的作品之一，属于15世纪初中国宫廷制作的一组图像。 此时，本身是佛教徒的永乐皇帝（1403-1424）与西藏宗教领袖之间的密切接触，导致了频繁的外交和宗教交流。 此图代表了生活在9世纪北印度的大乘禅师或伟大的瑜伽师维鲁帕。 来访的西藏人也收到了类似的图像，不过通常要小得多，目的是为了标记和巩固这种新建立的联盟关系。 他们在西藏被尊称为开悟的生命，并经常作为前往印度接受佛教启蒙的西藏人的老师而出现在西藏的传承中。
